review.blurb: You may occasionally find yourself longing for the levels and graphical style of the original game, but the new model doesn't disappoint in any way.
With the addition of a password save feature and new weapons, Blaster Master Enemy Below seeks to deliver a refreshing twist on a revered classic.
If you can deal with the lack of a traditional Bomberman multiplayer mode, the title makes a good candidate for your next portable game.
What one gets with Carmageddon is a game where every pro is met by an equally matched con.
For children from age 5 to 12, many fun hours of friendly haunting await. For adolescents and adults, however, there are better choices in the genre.
Don't be fooled into thinking that Catz (or its sister title, Dogz) is actually a game.
Chase H.Q.: Secret Police is fun to play, the strategy elements are engrossing, and the level design gives the game a sense of replay rarely seen in GBC racing titles.

games.title: Checkmate

review.blurb: This is one for serious chess heads who don't mind concentrating for hours on end. - Cameron Davis

review.blurb: Commander Keen was always better suited to a platform where instant save games could make up for its frantic gameplay and cranked difficulty.

games.title: Croc

review.blurb: Croc's characters are endearing, the level design is good, and the quest is both long and enjoyable. Unfortunately, the horrible control destroys the game's playability, making Croc for the Game Boy Color a different type of crock entirely. - Frank Provo

parse_issues: Earlier saved blurb was cut off mid-sentence; corrected against hub page

review.blurb: THQ has released a Croc game that lives up to the series' roots but doesn't exactly take the world by storm.
While the game is lacking in terms of overall gameplay, visual quality, and sound depth, there is never any doubt that you're playing a Cruis'n game.
For a game developed more than ten years ago, Crystalis is still surprisingly relevant, and it's a testament to tight, polished RPG game design.
Kemco transforms a reviled PC game into a highly playable Game Boy Color game.
It may not be perfect, but Dave Mirra Freestyle BMX plays well and looks awesome - two traits that will no doubt put it under many a tree this holiday season.
Dexter's Laboratory is founded on some classic gameplay, giving it the potential to please both fans of the show and fans of classic gaming.

games.title: Disney's The Little Mermaid II Pinball Frenzy
games.index_title: Disney's The Little Mermaid II Pinball Frenzy

review.blurb: Disney's The Little Mermaid II Pinball Frenzy is little more than a remake of Pokémon Pinball, minus Pikachu and his cohorts.
There's really nothing to do other than to turn your Game Boy on, watch your dog run around the screen, and wonder why you're wasting your time with this title.
Donkey Kong Country is one of the most playable and replayable Game Boy Color games ever created.
Dragon Warrior may seem like just an appetizer for the full-featured RPG experience in Dragon Warrior II, but the ability to play both games in succession and witness the interaction of their story
DWIII is a worthy port of its old NES ancestor, but its firm grounding in the RPG old-school means that only the hard-core need apply.
Eighteen years later, it's still a refreshingly innovative game.
Driving around is fun and exciting, the levels are varied, and the side games really do improve your skill within the main game.
With titles like Toy Story 2 and Gex 3 out for the Game Boy, Duke Nukem simply falls short.
Take last year's WWF Attitude, strip out the WWF license, insert the ECW characters, and voila - a new game to release in 2000.
Evel Knievel is all about precision - knowing when to tap what, how hard, and for how long is integral to making an enjoyable experience out of this game.
F1 Championship Season 2000 is about what you'd expect: An arcade-style racing game with a simulation twist that's amply capable of satisfying the F1 fan's pocket-gaming needs.

games.title: FIFA '98 - Road to the World Cup
games.index_title: FIFA '98 - Road to the World Cup

review.blurb: This is a great conversion of the 16- and 32-bit franchise of the same name.
The game could have been a modest success, as it has scores of teams to choose from, a bevy of options, and even an indoor soccer game that plays ten times faster than the regular form.
Frogger is one of those gaming archetypes that has remained basically unaltered since it made its coin-op debut.
If NES-caliber sound and graphics wrapped around one of the most memorable classic games fills you with nostalgia, then Frogger 2 for the Game Boy Color is right up your alley.
Fans of the genre or those who want to pick up a decent game that will keep them coming back for more won't be disappointed.
Overall, it's a great version of a real classic.

games.title: Gold and Glory: The Road to El Dorado
games.index_title: Gold and Glory: The Road to El Dorado

review.blurb: While the game's plot and gameplay are standard, it's eye-candy that El Dorado excels in. Miguel and Tulio walk, jump, crawl, and meander with countless frames of animation.
Harvest Moon is a relaxing and rewarding simulation of the simple life on the farm, combining all the things that made games like Tamagotchi and Pokemon such addictive hits and adding some charm
Heroes of Might and Magic is an average strategy game that tries very hard to bring as many aspects of the genre as it can to the Game Boy Color.

games.title: Indiana Jones and the Infernal Machine
games.index_title: Indiana Jones and the Infernal Machine

review.blurb: If it weren't for all of the pointless wandering and the lack of plot development, Indiana Jones and the Infernal Machine would have been a great game.
Konami's International Superstar Soccer series has been the pinnacle of soccer excellence on any other console it has graced, so the GB conversion arrives with plenty of high hopes attached.
Yes, Kirby Tilt 'n' Tumble is a gimmicky game, but it's a gimmicky game done well.

games.title: Legend of the River King 2

review.blurb: Although the game itself isn't overwhelmingly deep in terms of either fishing strategy or RPG intricacy, the incorporation of a number of Pokémon-inspired gameplay elements lends this easygoing adventure a charm that can't be overlooked. - Frank Provo

parse_issues: Earlier saved blurb was truncated at 200 chars; corrected against hub page

review.blurb: We can't urge you enough to play this game.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Ages
games.index_title: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Ages

review.blurb: Ages is a wonderful game in its own right, and as a set with Seasons, it comes as highly recommended as a game can be.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons
games.index_title: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons

review.blurb: Although Capcom's Flagship team actually handled development on the two games, both of them pack in everything one expects from a good Zelda adventure.
Unpleasant - that's the best word to describe Little Nicky.
Infogrames' Looney Tunes Collector: Alert! may not be Pokémon, but it's a finely polished puzzle-quest action-RPG nonetheless.
Looney Tunes Racing has a way to go before it can stack up to the big boys.
The control is dead-on, the graphics are clean, and there are enough options to keep you tossing the pigskin around for a long time.
Magical Tetris Challenge is a winner of a game.
Mario Golf is an excellent adaptation of the N64 title, and it's a Game Boy experience that stands well on its own.
A lot of polish went into Mario Tennis, and it shows.
The history of gaming is full of poor movie adaptations, and the Mask of Zorro represents one more.
Unless you've played Road Champs BXS Stunt Biking to death, the sheer number of gameplay and style improvements present in Mat Hoffman ultimately make it the more satisfying of the two games.
If you're a fan of the series, Xtreme's general gameplay, familiar environments, and visual repertoire should be enough to warrant a purchase.
It will certainly appeal to an audience eager for a serious challenge and more classic Mega Man action as well as those who might have been disappointed with the previous game.
The Men In Black franchise had such an opportunity to be a good video game - wild alien characters, cool weapons, stylish black suits - but what we have here is a complete waste of potential.
In all, Men In Black isn't a bad game, but it isn't entirely exciting.
Despite minor gripes, Metal Gear Solid is, without equal, the best tactical-espionage title on the Game Boy Color.
Metal Walker is a more than worthwhile endeavor for anyone that is in between Pokémon games.
With more than 20 tracks and six characters to choose from, this title shows how Game Boy racers should be done.
Varied gameplay, diverse options, gorgeous visuals, and ample two-player support make Mickey's Speedway USA a class-A title.

games.title: Micro Machines 1 and 2: Twin Turbo

review.blurb: Unlike recent games that attempt to imitate the gameplay and style of Micro Machines, Micro Machines 1 and 2: Twin Turbo proves that nothing can improve on a series that neared perfection to begin with. - Frank Provo

parse_issues: Earlier saved blurb was truncated at 200 chars; corrected against hub page

review.blurb: Mission: Impossible seems geared to those hard-core gamers out there who have both the time and the patience to spend replaying level after level until they've finished the game.
People looking for portable fighting-game action would do well to wait for Street Fighter Alpha, a much more responsive fighting game.
If you're the type of person who can forgive a lack of features for an otherwise impeccable game, Mr. Driller might be a decent addition to your puzzle game library.

games.title: The Mummy

review.blurb: Fans of spatially oriented puzzle games won't christen it the second coming of Solomon's Key, but there's enough challenge and intelligence within each of The Mummy's 46 stages to keep most people occupied for a goodly amount of time. - Frank Provo

parse_issues: Earlier saved blurb was cut off mid-sentence; corrected against hub page

review.blurb: Offering 33 unique cars, 16 tracks, real-life drivers, a season mode, a variety of car-tuning options, and a two-player link-cable option, THQ has crammed a great deal into this pocket-sized beauty.
NASCAR Challenge is a dull racing game that doesn't have much going for it.
If you've ever wondered what Micro Machines would be like with NASCAR drivers, Majesco's NASCAR Heat is the answer.
If it weren't for its abhorrent background music, tinny sound effects, and lack of a two-player feature, NBA Hoopz would be a glowing addition to the Game Boy Color's library.
NBA Jam 99 on the Game Boy Color takes the series back to the two-on-two arcade action that it is famous for.
Even hard-core hockey fans should avoid this title; it will start gathering dust on its first day of play.
Perfect Dark GBC does its Nintendo 64 counterpart justice, albeit haphazardly.
For those who are new to Pokémon or have yet to upgrade from the Red/Blue/Yellow series, Pokémon: Crystal Version offers a great deal of value for the investment involved.
You really can't go wrong with 251 monsters, two main adventures, countless side quests, and a baseline of 60 hours of gameplay.
Pokemon Pinball manages the impossible by being more than a shameless cash-in on the Pokemon phenomenon.
Pokémon Puzzle Challenge is a game that does the Pokémon license proud.
You really can't go wrong with 251 monsters, two main adventures, countless side quests, and a baseline of 60 hours of gameplay.
A great game for a time, Pokemon Trading Card is a faithful and amusing adaptation of the collectible card game, but it suffers as a single-player video game.
At the outset, Polaris SnoCross is an above-average racer that delivers the "extreme" experience, while including an oft-neglected link-play feature.

games.title: Powerpuff Girls Episode 1: Bad Mojo Jojo
games.index_title: Powerpuff Girls Episode 1: Bad Mojo Jojo

review.blurb: Fans of the Cartoon Network's Powerpuff Girls series will ultimately be disappointed by Bad Mojo Jojo since the game is extremely simple and boring.
Project S-11 is about the best the GBC is going to see in terms of space shooters.
R-Type DX is one of the best shooters you can get for any machine, and the GBC version does the series proud.
If your idea of a good time is blowing things up, Metal Gear Solid or Army Men might be better choices.

games.title: Rayman

review.blurb: One of the better titles to hit the Game Boy Color in recent history.

review.blurb: Resident Evil Gaiden doesn't inspire the same level of interest that the other games in the franchise do.
Surprisingly, the game isn't just an attempt to cash in on a passing trend - it's also a decent addition to any stunt-bike aficionado's collection.
As an action game, Roswell Conspiracies is rather basic, but the plot is certainly fanciful enough to appeal to less discerning consumers.
Rugrats: The Movie for the Game Boy is the only way you can relive the surprise hit without buying a VCR
Visually, aurally, and in terms of gameplay, there's nothing good about this version of Rush 2049.
The game is brief, but the tale it tells provides plenty of classic Scooby-Doo antics.
Classic gaming fanatics will eat it up, but fussier gamers would be more satisfied elsewhere.
Shadowgate Classic has is that it has not improved with age, and newcomers will fail to see the original charm hidden under the unintuitive gameplay.
Shantae is a fine example of how good a 2D platform game can be on a portable system.
The lack of moves, strategy, and a two-player mode limits the game's appeal.

games.title: The Simpsons: Night of the Living Treehouse of Horror
games.index_title: The Simpsons: Night of the Living Treehouse of Horror

review.blurb: THQ has managed to re-create a decade of Halloween specials into a single GBC game that's bound to give series fans hours of recreation.
There are inevitably going to be a dozen or so average platformers in your Game Boy collection, one of them might as well be this.

More fully realized than anything on the 8- or 16-bit systems, Spider-Man for the GBC is the game we all wish we had ten years ago - a totally convincing interpretation of Spidey for the handheld sector.
Even though it's only a subtle remake, fans of the webbed wonder will no doubt enjoy everything that Spider-Man 2: The Sinister Six has to offer.

games.title: SpongeBob SquarePants: Legend of the Lost Spatula
games.index_title: SpongeBob SquarePants: Legend of the Lost Spatula

review.blurb: There is no evidence to suggest that children would actually enjoy playing a game this unremarkable--let alone adults.
Spy Vs. Spy is a fast-paced, comedic strategy title especially suited for the more vindictive of players.
Racer for the Game Boy Color is a fun little game.
Street Fighter Alpha stands alone as the best fighting game to ever hit the Game Boy.
It looks like we finally have the "killer app" for the Game Boy Color.
Tech Deck Skateboarding is a solid video game re-creation of the uniquely hands-on Tech Deck experience.
In all, what really makes Cycles a good game is the balance of arcade-style gameplay and a lengthy championship mode.
What you get with Test Drive Le Mans is the most solid GBC racing title to date. The features are thick, the gameplay is deep, and the level of replay isn't contrived.
Tetris has been often called the greatest game ever created, and the Game Boy version is the best version of Russia's greatest export.
Tom and Jerry: Mouse Hunt is a fun and exciting sportslike game that lives up the TV show's madcap, albeit sometimes violent, reputation.
As a total package, Tomb Raider for Game Boy Color delivers a degree of immersion not realized since Tomb Raider 2.

games.title: Tomb Raider: Curse of the Sword
games.index_title: Tomb Raider: Curse of the Sword

review.blurb: If you found the previous pocket-sized Tomb Raider too sluggish or bland, this new one probably won't change your mind.
If R/C Pro-Am didn't exist, this game would probably be taken a bit more seriously.
Though there's much room for improvement, Tony Hawk Pro Skater is easily the best skateboarding game available for the Game Boy Color. - Frank Provo
Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 is a must buy for any handheld-boarding fan.
Some will be drawn to the quirky, skills-type gameplay, while others may find Toobin's innovative ideas buried under a sea of unforgiving control and limited replay value.
With so many exceptional Game Boy platformers on the market, one simply can't justify picking up Toonsylvania.
Top Gear Pocket feels like a Sunday drive.
The average gamer just isn't going to find Towers' quest all that engaging or exciting.
If the designers had done their homework and played the original Super Mario Bros. game they would have realized that it's never a good idea to make the jump button the same as the run button.
The 3D visuals and cartoon-style charm contained within Toy Story Racer do make it an excellent choice for children, Disney fans, or Game Boy fanatics who enjoy visual gimmicks.

games.title: Triple Play 2001

review.blurb: Triple Play 2001 is a perfect example of how good ideas can go horribly awry. - Frank Provo

review.blurb: Despite being a rehash, Turok 3 is a well-balanced, varied platform gaming experience.
If you're looking for a high-quality action game, you can't go wrong with this one.
There is definitely some fun to be had here.
In every category, be it gameplay, sound, visuals, or replay, Infogrames' Wacky Races turns in a solid performance.
As far as platformers go, Wario Land 3 is a game that fires on all cylinders.
Wario Land II DX is one of the best 2D platformers to come out of Nintendo in years.
New or younger players should be able to look past the game's limitations and simply accept it as a simple but fun game.
WCW Mayhem marks a respectable entry for EA into the realm of handheld wrestling titles.
While the game is, in its little digital soul, a side-scrolling shooter, it really, really wants to be a simulation.
If you're looking for clever courses, brutal power-ups, and plenty of replay, look no further than Woody Woodpecker Racing.
It's better than the wrestling games to come before it, but WWF Attitude still doesn't quite get the job done.
Double Dragon it's not, but WWF Betrayal does give you the chance to pummel hoodlums and machine-gun-toting businessmen with reckless abandon.
While the "big brother" console release of X-Men: Mutant Academy may be at least tolerable, the Game Boy Color release falls flat.
X-Men: Mutant Wars is an archetypical example of a good idea executed badly.
Discerning action aficionados require much more than the 13 brief levels of slashing, jumping, and supernatural healing that this game has to offer
Xtreme Sports is definitely going to be an unsung hit.
Sadly, there is no reason for anyone to play through Yoda Stories.
Dark Duel Stories comes recommended to avid enthusiasts of the Duel Monsters card game.

games.title: Dragon Warrior Monsters

review.blurb: If you've already "caught 'em all," and you're looking for a game to tide you over until Pokemon Gold and Silver are released near the end of the year, Dragon Warrior Monsters is exactly what you're looking for. - Jeff Gerstmann

review.blurb: Even though the gameplay is solid, the bland visuals and lackluster sound make 1942 a tough pill to swallow.

games.title: Action Man: Search for Base X
games.index_title: Action Man: Search for Base X

review.blurb: While the game could be a touch easier and a tad less repetitive, it's still a fine addition to the 2D action genre.
About the only people capable of enjoying Airforce Delta will be Afterburner or Blue Lightning junkies seeking their latest pseudo-3D flying fix.
In execution, Alice offers some of the best graphics and gameplay ever seen on a portable system.

Due to limitations in graphical and sound capabilities, handheld baseball titles still have a long way to go before they catch up to their console counterparts. Acclaim's All-Star Baseball 2001 is a step in the right direction.
Antz on the GBC is another platform game that will amuse those who find the genre enjoyable in small scale 8-bit.
Taken as a whole, Army Men is an enjoyable game that delivers the pleasingly nostalgic experience of plastic-soldier warfare.
IMPORT: Asterix: The Search for Dogmatix is one of the better combinations of platformer and plot to come out in recent years.
While this title isn't going to win any awards, it's a satisfying way to spend some free time.
Ballistic is a simple and fun game with a fairly innovative puzzle mechanic that's at least good for a while.

Batman: Chaos in Gotham does well by following a storyline that would have appeared in the comic book or animated series and dressed it up with an assortment of gaming styles and a deep level of control. - Trevor Rivers
